title: lifedraft input contract — universal $defs: the estate block
$comment: Fragment of the universal input contract, merged into schema/input_schema.json by input_contract.load_universal_schema() -- see that function and compose_schema() for the exact, total merge rule. This file is a FRAGMENT, not a standalone schema: its "#/$defs/..." references resolve only in the composed document. Estate FACTS in force: the estate record, its rollover election override and the life-insurance policies. Mortality is a BELIEF and lives in assumptions.json instead.

renewal_end_date.description: Issue #138: declared term RENEWAL -- coverage continues past term_end_date to this date (the insurer's renewal premium is set by the insurer at renewal and is NOT modelled; only the declared premium_annual through term_end_date is priced). Must be strictly after term_end_date; null/absent means the policy LAPSES at term_end_date -- the death benefit leaves the estate and the premium stops. Refused on a permanent policy (term_end_date null): a policy with no term does not renew.

rollover_override.$comment: x-uncertainty on .spousal_rollover below: same domain question as estate.default_spousal_rollover, asked per-account (#671).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Read the will and this account's beneficiary designation.
x-uncertainty.question: Is a spousal rollover elected on this specific account?

default_spousal_rollover.description: The spousal-rollover election in force by default for every account with a spousal beneficiary/successor_holder (in Canada: ITA s.146(8.1)/s.70(6)). Not rolling over is sometimes optimal (uses the first spouse's low brackets) — this is a FACT about what the current will/beneficiary designations say, not a decision; the sweep across rollover-vs-not lives in decisions.estate_elections. THIS IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES 'not rolling over' EXPRESSIBLE — #600's headline six-figure silent assumption.
